concepts.note: Below a critical temperature, a superconductor carries current without measurable resistive dissipation.
concepts.title: Zero resistance

concepts.note: A superconductor expels magnetic flux from its interior, distinguishing it from a perfect conductor.
concepts.title: Meissner effect

concepts.note: Phenomenological electrodynamics relates supercurrent to the vector potential and predicts a penetration depth λ_L.
concepts.title: London equations

concepts.note: Abrikosov (1957) predicted quantized magnetic flux vortices in type-II superconductors above the lower critical field.
concepts.title: Type-II vortices

subtopics.note: Onnes discovered zero resistance in mercury below 4.2 K in 1911, and the Meissner–Ochsenfeld effect (1933) showed flux expulsion, captured by the London equation ∇²B = B/λ_L².
subtopics.title: Superconductivity

concepts.note: Periodic potentials produce Bloch waves whose crystal momentum k is a good quantum number.
concepts.title: Bloch theorem

concepts.note: Bragg scattering at zone boundaries opens gaps and organizes electronic states into bands.
concepts.title: Band gap and Brillouin zone

concepts.note: Near a band extremum, an electron responds as a free particle with mass m* set by band curvature.
concepts.title: Effective mass

concepts.note: Wilson (1931) distinguished metals from insulators by partially filled versus filled bands.
concepts.title: Wilson metal-insulator classification

subtopics.note: Bloch's theorem (1928) shows that electrons in a periodic potential have wavefunctions ψ_k(r) = e^{ik·r} u_k(r), so allowed energies form bands separated by gaps. Wilson's 1931 classification used filled and empty bands to explain metals, insulators and semiconductors.
subtopics.title: Band theory and Bloch theorem

concepts.note: Donor or acceptor impurities make n-type or p-type semiconductors with tunable conductivity.
concepts.title: Doping and carrier type

concepts.note: A depletion region and built-in field give asymmetric current–voltage rectification.
concepts.title: p–n junction

concepts.note: The first transistor used two closely spaced metal contacts on germanium to amplify signals.
concepts.title: Point-contact transistor

concepts.note: The metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor became the scalable building block of integrated circuits.
concepts.title: MOSFET scaling

subtopics.note: Doping controls electron or hole carriers, and a p–n junction rectifies current according to the Shockley diode equation I = I₀ (e^{eV/k_BT} − 1). Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley's 1947 point-contact transistor at Bell Labs launched solid-state electronics.
subtopics.title: Semiconductors and transistor

concepts.note: Two electrons near the Fermi surface form a bound pair for an arbitrarily weak attractive interaction.
concepts.title: Cooper pairs

concepts.note: Lattice polarization screens Coulomb repulsion and provides a retarded attraction between electrons.
concepts.title: Phonon-mediated attraction

concepts.note: Breaking a pair costs energy Δ, producing an activated excitation spectrum and exponential specific heat.
concepts.title: BCS energy gap

concepts.note: T_c depends on ionic mass as M^{−α}, supporting the phonon mechanism.
concepts.title: Isotope effect

subtopics.note: Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer (1957) showed that a phonon-mediated attraction binds electrons into Cooper pairs, which condense into a gapped ground state. The weak-coupling gap is Δ ≈ 2ħω_D exp[−1/(N(0)V)].
subtopics.title: BCS theory

concepts.note: Systems sharing dimension and symmetry have the same critical exponents.
concepts.title: Universality classes

concepts.note: Near T_c, the free energy is a homogeneous function of reduced temperature and field.
concepts.title: Scaling hypothesis

concepts.note: Iterative coarse-graining flows to fixed points and yields scaling laws.
concepts.title: Wilson renormalization group

concepts.note: Wilson and Fisher computed exponents near four dimensions in powers of ε = 4 − d.
concepts.title: Epsilon expansion

subtopics.note: Continuous phase transitions show power-law divergences such as ξ ∝ |T − T_c|^{−ν}, with exponents set by universality rather than microscopic details. Wilson's renormalization group (1971) explains this via fixed points of scale transformations.
subtopics.title: Phase transitions and RG

concepts.note: von Klitzing observed exact σ_xy = ν e²/h plateaus in 1980.
concepts.title: Integer quantum Hall effect

concepts.note: Tsui and Störmer observed ν = 1/3 in 1982; Laughlin's wavefunction (1983) described it.
concepts.title: Fractional quantum Hall effect

concepts.note: Cyclotron motion is quantized as E_n = ħω_c(n + 1/2).
concepts.title: Landau levels

concepts.note: Chiral edge modes and a Chern number make the quantization robust against disorder.
concepts.title: Topological edge states

subtopics.note: In a strong perpendicular magnetic field, a two-dimensional electron gas exhibits quantized Hall conductance σ_xy = ν e²/h and vanishing longitudinal resistance. Integer (1980) and fractional (1982) plateaus arise from Landau-level filling, disorder, and topological edge states.
subtopics.title: Quantum Hall effect

concepts.note: Layered copper oxides show high Tc and strong electronic anisotropy.
concepts.title: Cuprate discovery

concepts.note: Phase-sensitive measurements indicate a sign-changing d_{x²−y²} gap.
concepts.title: d-wave pairing

concepts.note: A partial gap persists above Tc, suggesting competing or precursor order.
concepts.title: Pseudogap

concepts.note: Iron-based superconductors (Hosono, 2008) and high-pressure hydrides such as H₃S at 203 K (Eremets, 2015) extended the search for higher Tc.
concepts.title: Beyond cuprates

subtopics.note: Bednorz and Müller discovered superconductivity near 35 K in La–Ba–Cu–O in 1986, and cuprates soon exceeded the 77 K boiling point of nitrogen. The pairing mechanism and pseudogap remain central open questions.
subtopics.title: High-Tc cuprates

concepts.note: The honeycomb lattice gives linear bands at the K and K′ points.
concepts.title: Graphene Dirac cones

concepts.note: Bulk band inversion yields conducting edge or surface states protected by symmetry.
concepts.title: Topological insulators

concepts.note: A bulk Chern or Z₂ invariant counts the protected boundary modes.
concepts.title: Bulk-boundary correspondence

concepts.note: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts correlated insulators and superconductivity near the magic angle.
concepts.title: Moiré flat bands

subtopics.note: Graphene was isolated in 2004, and its low-energy electrons obey H = v_F σ·k, a massless Dirac equation. Topological invariants then classified gapped phases with protected edge states, while twisted bilayers (2018) produced flat bands and correlated phases.
subtopics.title: Topological and 2D materials
